grading_contract.required: Every required meaning must be represented; labels/cards/views/edges/grouping may vary. No mandatory exact node count or names. Source citations do not substitute for omitted behavior.
grading_contract.optional: Do not fail for optional details; if asserted they must agree with the pinned source.
grading_contract.scope: No runtime execution required for static source description; dynamic external behavior must remain a boundary. No unsupported implementation claims.
grading_contract.first_final: Review first and final independently; source-range checks and semantic entailment are separate.
grading_contract.visual: Same 1440x900 initial viewport. Important roles/labels/relations must be readable; record below-fold content as overview limitation, not permanent clipping without evidence.

required: Public instance/method/default merging leads to Ky.create and per-request Ky construction; configured request/normalized options feed later work.
beforeRequest can replace Request or supply Response, allowing the fetch attempt to be bypassed; normal attempts reach the configured/native fetch boundary.

Retry logic decides eligibility and delay using retry limit and relevant method/error policy, then runs beforeRetry before another attempt; it is conditional, not every failure unconditionally retried.
beforeRetry can replace Request, provide Response, or stop work; returned responses and normal fetched responses pass through afterResponse handling, which can change the response or request a retry.

HTTP failure handling is conditional on throwHttpErrors and response circumstances; terminal errors flow through the implemented final error processing boundary while successful results return the response.
Per-attempt/remaining total timeout and user cancellation constrain work; native Fetch/Request/Response and user hook behavior are external boundaries, not invented server/database internals.
truth_if_asserted: User abort is surfaced rather than reclassified as a retryable network error.
Forced afterResponse retry can bypass ordinary method/shouldRetry checks but still respects retry budget.
HTTP errors from hook-supplied responses do not enter the same automatic retry path as ordinary fetched HTTP errors.
beforeRequest hooks are before the retry loop; they are not rerun before every retry attempt.
beforeError does not indiscriminately transform every possible thrown value; use actual implementation boundaries.
optional: init hooks and their cloned options

required: QueryClient.fetchQuery applies defaults, uses QueryCache.build to get/create a Query by hash, and returns existing data when fresh or starts Query.fetch when stale.
QueryCache owns storage/reuse of Query instances; Query owns execution state and observers, rather than QueryClient directly running native network I/O.
An already active fetch can reuse the retryer promise; execution wraps a caller-supplied queryFn/context and exposes cancellation via AbortSignal without claiming the callback always honors it.
Retryer controls attempt execution, retry eligibility/delay and pause/continue conditions using focus/online/network mode; fetchQuery defaults retry to false if unspecified at this revision.
Success sets data/state and runs supported cache success/settled notifications; terminal error/cancellation branches are distinguished and ordinary failures update error state and rethrow.
Query state dispatch uses notifyManager.batch to notify observers and QueryCache subscribers; batching control is not a new worker/network service.
truth_if_asserted: cancelRefetch requires the stated data/options conditions; all concurrent fetches are not automatically cancelled.
Cancellation may be silent or revert state according to options; AbortSignal does not guarantee cancellation of arbitrary user work.
The configured queryFn, custom behavior/persister and framework callbacks are external extension points, not hardcoded implementations.
notifyManager.batch invokes the callback synchronously; scheduled callback batching and scheduler behavior are distinct.
optional: Exact retry default in generic retryer versus fetchQuery override
Cache mounting and browser event listener setup

required: add wraps the caller task in a promise-producing queued run and enqueues it in the configured/default priority queue; PQueue owns scheduling while the task implementation remains an external callable.
Waiting queue contents and active pending count are different state; admission needs unpaused state and both concurrency and interval allowance before dequeue/invocation.
A running task settles the returned promise on success/error, emits the supported terminal notification, and finally schedules capacity release/next admission.
pause prevents starting queued work and start resumes admission; it does not retroactively terminate active tasks.
A waiting aborted task is removed with the supported queue capability and rejects; a running task races abort and receives the signal, but its underlying work needs cooperation.
Execution timeout begins around the invoked operation, not while waiting, and can reject without proving the underlying external task stopped.
truth_if_asserted: PriorityQueue chooses higher priorities first and keeps FIFO among equal priorities.
Custom queue removal on waiting abort is best-effort when remove is supported, not guaranteed for every arbitrary queueClass.
The interval timer can reopen admission; concurrency and interval limits are separate.
The library is an in-process Promise queue, not a distributed/durable broker.
optional: Exact event order beyond primary settlement and next-admission relation
